h1: Extra Virgin Olive Oil Salad Dressing: Ratios and Method
excerpt: An extra virgin olive oil salad dressing is three parts oil to one part acid, an emulsifier, and a slow pour. Everything else is a variation on that.
keyTakeaway: An extra virgin olive oil salad dressing is three parts oil to one part acid by volume, held together by mustard, honey or crushed garlic and a slow whisked pour. Dissolve the salt in the acid first. Keep the rest in a capped glass jar in the fridge and shake it back together.
heroAlt: A bottle of Arabian Village olive oil standing upright on a wooden table, whole olives and olive leaves scattered around its base, daylight coming from the side.
inlineAlt: Seen from above: a white ceramic bowl of mixed green salad leaves on a wooden table, beside a small glass jug of olive oil and a lemon half.
intro: A salad dressing is the shortest recipe in the kitchen and one of the easiest to get wrong, usually because the oil hit the bowl before the salt had dissolved. Three ingredients, one order of operations, ninety seconds.
Below: the ratios, a whisking method that holds, the faults that split a dressing, four builds, and how long a jar keeps.

blocks.text: A vinaigrette starts at three parts oil to one part acid, measured by volume. Three tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil to one tablespoon of lemon juice dresses a bowl of leaves for four. Shift to 2:1 on sturdy leaves, and to 4:1 when the vinegar is strong.

sections.heading: How to make the emulsion hold

blocks.text: Oil and acid do not dissolve in one another, so something has to hold them suspended. A teaspoon of Dijon mustard, half a teaspoon of honey, or a garlic clove crushed to a paste with salt will each do it. Order matters more than the whisk.

items: Stir the acid, salt and pepper together until the salt dissolves. Salt will not dissolve in oil.
Whisk in the mustard, honey or garlic paste.
Pour the oil in a thin stream, whisking without stopping, until it thickens and turns opaque.
Taste it on a leaf, not off the spoon: more oil if it bites, more acid if it sits flat.

sections.heading: What goes wrong, and the fix

blocks.text: Almost every failed dressing is one of four things: the oil went in too fast, the salt never dissolved, there was no emulsifier, or the leaves were wet from the tap. A split dressing still rebuilds — whisk fresh mustard in a clean bowl and pour the split mixture in slowly.

items: **Split at once.** No emulsifier. Rebuild it onto mustard or garlic paste.
**Harsh.** Too much acid, or salt added last. Add oil a teaspoon at a time.
**Flat.** Wet leaves dilute whatever lands on them. Spin or pat them dry.
**Solid in the fridge.** Normal. Twenty minutes on the counter reverses it.

sections.heading: Which oil, and when to pour it

blocks.text: A dressing is an unheated use, so the oil's own character lands on the plate rather than being cooked off. Extra virgin is the grade that has one: green, fruity, peppery at the back of the throat. Refined pure and light grades are processed to taste of almost nothing. For where that character comes from, read [what cold-pressed olive oil really means](/blog/what-cold-pressed-olive-oil-really-means).
Dress at the table. Salt and acid draw water from a leaf within minutes.

sections.heading: Four dressings on the same base

blocks.text: Four dressings run off one base: three parts extra virgin olive oil to one part acid, the salt dissolved in the acid first, the oil whisked in last. Lemon and garlic, mustard vinaigrette, balsamic, and calamansi with soy each change a single ingredient. The quantities dress a bowl for four.

items: **Lemon and garlic.** 3 tbsp oil, 1 tbsp lemon juice, one clove crushed with salt, black pepper. For cucumber and tomato.
**Mustard vinaigrette.** 3 tbsp oil, 1 tbsp red wine vinegar, 1 tsp Dijon, a little honey. For romaine and boiled egg.
**Balsamic.** 4 tbsp oil, 1 tbsp balsamic vinegar, salt. For tomato, rocket and anything with cheese.
**Calamansi and soy.** 3 tbsp oil, 1 tbsp calamansi juice, 1 tsp light soy sauce. For shredded cabbage and mango.

sections.heading: What to keep it in and how long it keeps

blocks.text: A screw-top glass jar is the whole storage answer: mix in it, pour from it, cap the rest and shake it back together. Plain oil, vinegar and mustard keeps about two weeks in the refrigerator, and anything fresh stirred in cuts that to a few days.
Three parts oil, one part acid, the salt dissolved in the acid first, mustard or garlic to hold it, the oil poured last in a thin stream. Keep the rest capped in the fridge.

faqs.q: What is the ratio of olive oil to vinegar in a salad dressing?
faqs.a: Three parts oil to one part vinegar by volume: three tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil to one tablespoon of vinegar. Use 2:1 for a sharper dressing on sturdy leaves, and 4:1 when the vinegar is strong.

faqs.q: Can I use extra virgin olive oil for salad dressing?
faqs.a: Yes, and a dressing is the use that shows it best. Nothing is heated, so the fruit, bitterness and peppery finish reach the plate intact. Refined pure and light grades are processed to taste of very little.

faqs.q: Why does my olive oil dressing separate?
faqs.a: Oil and acid do not dissolve in one another, so a dressing with no emulsifier separates within a minute. A teaspoon of mustard, a little honey, or garlic crushed to a paste with salt holds them together.

faqs.q: How do I fix a dressing that has split?
faqs.a: Whisk a fresh teaspoon of Dijon mustard in a clean bowl, then pour the split dressing into it in a thin stream, whisking throughout. It comes back together. Pouring the oil too fast is the usual cause.

faqs.q: How long does homemade salad dressing keep?
faqs.a: Oil, vinegar, mustard and salt keeps about two weeks in a capped jar in the fridge. Raw garlic or shallot brings that to three or four days, soft herbs to two or three, yogurt or tahini to two.

faqs.q: Why does my dressing go solid in the fridge?
faqs.a: Olive oil clouds and turns semi-solid at fridge temperature, which is normal rather than a fault. Take the jar out about twenty minutes before the meal and shake it back together before pouring.
